record.original_question: For a Dupin hypersurface M contained in a hypersphere, when is M of finite type, and when does finite type force M to be isoparametric?

evidence.quote: Problem 4. When is a Dupin hypersurface M of a hypersphere of finite type? When is a finite type Dupin hypersurface of a hypersphere isoparametric?

artifact.category_tag: Dupin hypersurfaces and finite type submanifolds
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^{n}\subset\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ denote the unit hypersphere, and let $M^{n-1}\subset S^{n}$ be a smooth, connected, oriented hypersurface. Recall the following notions.

(i) A curvature surface of $M$ is a connected submanifold $N\subset M$ such that for each $p\in N$, the tangent space $T_pN$ is equal to a smooth principal curvature distribution (an eigenspace of the shape operator). $M$ is called a Dupin hypersurface if along every curvature surface $N$ the corresponding principal curvature is constant. $M$ is called proper Dupin if, in addition, the number $g$ of distinct principal curvatures is constant on $M$, and each principal curvature has constant multiplicity.

(ii) $M$ is said to be isoparametric (in $S^{n}$) if all its principal curvatures are globally constant on $M$.

(iii) Let $x:M\to\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ be the inclusion and $\Delta$ the Laplace–Beltrami operator of the induced metric. The submanifold $M$ is said to be of finite type if its position vector $x$ admits a finite spectral decomposition
$$x = x_0 + x_{t_1} + x_{t_2} + \cdots + x_{t_k},$$
where $x_0$ is a constant vector in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, $k$ is a positive integer, and each $x_{t_i}:M\to\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ is a non-constant smooth map satisfying $\Delta x_{t_i}=\lambda_{t_i}x_{t_i}$ for distinct real eigenvalues $\lambda_{t_1}<\lambda_{t_2}<\cdots<\lambda_{t_k}$. The smallest such $k$ is the type of $M$. (Isoparametric hypersurfaces of $S^n$ are known to be of finite type.)

Resolve the following two questions:

(a) Give a characterization (necessary and sufficient geometric conditions) for a (proper) Dupin hypersurface $M\subset S^{n}$ to be of finite type.

(b) Determine whether every (compact, proper) Dupin hypersurface of $S^{n}$ that is of finite type must be isoparametric, and if not, classify all finite-type Dupin hypersurfaces in $S^{n}$ which fail to be isoparametric.
artifact.status_search_result: The two questions appear to remain open in general. They are explicitly recorded as unresolved problems in surveys on Dupin and isoparametric hypersurfaces, and recent work (e.g., classification of compact proper Dupin hypersurfaces with constant Lie curvatures, and constructions of compact Dupin hypersurfaces with non-constant Lie curvatures) has not produced a general characterization of the finite-type condition for Dupin hypersurfaces of a sphere or shown that finite type forces isoparametricity. No source found announces a complete solution.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on Isoparametric Hypersurfaces and Their Generalizations
status_evidence.snippet: Survey treating the relationship between Dupin and isoparametric hypersurfaces, listing open problems including those on finite type.
status_evidence.claim: The relation between Dupin hypersurfaces and isoparametric hypersurfaces, and questions about which Dupin hypersurfaces are forced to be isoparametric, remain a topic of ongoing research.

status_evidence.title: Constructions of Compact Dupin Hypersurfaces with Non-constant Lie Curvatures
status_evidence.snippet: Recent constructions show new compact proper Dupin hypersurfaces, indicating the classification problem is far from complete.
status_evidence.claim: New examples continue to be constructed, suggesting the finite-type/isoparametric question is not settled.

status_evidence.title: Classifications of Dupin hypersurfaces in Lie sphere geometry
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of partial classification results for Dupin hypersurfaces in Lie sphere geometry; full classification not achieved.
status_evidence.claim: A general characterization of finite-type Dupin hypersurfaces of a hypersphere has not yet been obtained.

status_evidence.title: When is a finite type Dupin hypersurface of a hypersphere isoparametric? (ResearchGate)
status_evidence.snippet: The question is posed as an open problem on a research forum.
status_evidence.claim: The question of when a finite-type Dupin hypersurface of a hypersphere is isoparametric is publicly listed as an open problem.
